subject.title: Intermittent 30+ minute workspace-sandbox prep on cold-start (5.19-beta.1)

question: Should OpenClaw make Docker sandbox prep fail fast by default, and should that deadline cover prune, config-hash inspection, container init, and Docker user resolution or wait for a live OrbStack repro first?
rationale: The source-backed bug is real enough to keep open, but the final timeout scope, default behavior, config exposure, and fail-soft semantics can change existing slow-Docker operator workflows.

options.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
options.body: Preserve current skill mount propagation, bound the full prune/hash/init Docker control-plane path, document the default/config behavior, and require redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

options.title: Prove the OrbStack substep first
options.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer/live repro work until logs or a controlled macOS/OrbStack run identifies whether Docker exec, prune, workspace layout, or user resolution is actually responsible.

options.title: Decline a default timeout
options.body: Keep current behavior and document operator workarounds only if maintainers decide slow Docker control-plane waits should not become sandbox failures by default.

recommendation.title: Refresh or replace the timeout PR
recommendation.body: Preserve current skill mount propagation, bound the full prune/hash/init Docker control-plane path, document the default/config behavior, and require redacted real Docker or OrbStack proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox architecture, prune/runtime cleanup, and product compatibility boundaries where this handle has the strongest path-history signal.
